newsitem.title: USA: Lehman cuts stocks in recommended asset allocation.
newsitem.headline: Lehman cuts stocks in recommended asset allocation.

text.p: Lehman Bros chief investment strategist Jeffrey Applegate said in a research note that he had lowered his recommended exposure to stocks to 65 percent of asset allocation from 70 percent.
Exposure to bonds was increased to 35 percent from 30 percent.

"With the sharp rise in the equity market so far this year, the relative value of stocks to bonds has shifted. The stock-to-bond ratio has the equity market some 11 percent overvalued. The forward earnings yield gap has also turned against the equity market," he said in the note.
He said 1996 earnings "appear to be coming about in line with our estimate of $11.22 (for the S&P 500 stocks) for the fourth quarter ($41.25 for the entire year)."
"We are comfortable with our 1997 EPS of $45.00 and a forward price-earnings (ratio) estimate for the end of 1997 of 16.1," he said.
